newsitem.title: GERMANY: DASA says Airbus net profit fell in '96.
newsitem.headline: DASA says Airbus net profit fell in '96.

text.p: Daimler-Benz Aerospace (DASA), the German partner in the four-country Airbus consortium, on Wednesday confirmed that the European plane maker made a net profit of 707 million marks ($410.1 million) last year.
Corrected extracts from DASA's annual report showed profits were down from 855 million marks the year before. Sales in 1996 were 13.35 billion marks, down from 13.87 billion.
Airbus, which groups DASA, France's Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain, has traditionally kept its earnings a secret.

A DASA spokesman said the new profit figure had been released simply to correct the initial figure of over one billion marks published last month. "This was a simple calculating error which emerged later," the spokesman said.
He added DASA was publishing the figure in order to comply with U.S. accounting standards required under the listing of its parent, auto maker Daimler-Benz AG, on the New York Stock Exchange.
DASA's Hamburg-based Airbus unit made a profit of 1.44 billion marks last year, compared to a loss of 371 million marks in 1995, the figures showed.

Earlier, the Wall Street Journal reported that the figures came at a sensitive time for the members of the Airbus group, which are holding difficult negotiations on restructuring the loose consortium into a limited liability company by 1999.
But the DASA spokesman said there was "absolutely no connection" between the release of the figure and the talks.
-- Douglas Busvine, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.723 German Marks)
